description: Who a biblical name actually belongs to. Returns the distinct individuals and places bearing a name — each with its own identity, description, tribe or nation, family (parents, siblings, partners, offspring, every one carrying the related person's identity so you can look them up in turn), and the verses they appear in. Places carry coordinates. CALL THIS WHENEVER A QUESTION IS ABOUT A PERSON OR PLACE RATHER THAN A WORD: who someone was, whose son or daughter, who they married, where they appear, whether two mentions are the same man. CRITICAL: many biblical names are shared by several unrelated people — one name in this data covers twenty-nine different men — so this tool returns ALL of them and you must not assume the famous one is meant. If the question concerns a particular verse, match that verse against each individual's references before answering, and if it stays ambiguous, say so. Uncertainty in the source is preserved deliberately: a '(?)' marks a relationship the data itself is unsure of, and 'Unnamed#N' is a person Scripture never names — report both as they stand rather than smoothing them over. For what a WORD means or where it came from, use get_word_origin instead.

identity.description: The exact identity string of one individual, e.g. "Joseph@Gen.30.24-Rev", as returned by a previous call. Use this to get one person's family and full reference list.

name.description: English name as it appears in Scripture, e.g. "Zechariah".

name: get_person
